column1: # policy/ops/ops-hosts.tsv — THE PINNED AUTHORITY TABLE (operator host classes).
# THE AUTHOR IS THE OPERATOR, exactly like ops-aliases.tsv: this table is the
# bridge across the vocabulary seam for the AUTHORITY dimension — the
# host-tool http_get's classed argument is its `url`, and what the policy can
# say about a url is which CLASS its AUTHORITY (the host, normalized: scheme
# dropped, host lowercased, port dropped) belongs to, and whether that class
# is PROTECTED (which is what policy rule D3 consumes, through the SAME
# touches/class/protected facts and the SAME hosttool(W) bridge a host_cat
# path rides — there is deliberately NO second predicate and NO second policy
# path).
# Columns (TAB-separated; '#' starts a comment):
#   pattern     the HOST pattern.  THE GRAMMAR IS TWO FORMS, STATED AND
#               ENFORCED AT PIN TIME (eval_ops.py --check-hosts):
#                 * an EXACT host: no glob characters; matches that one host
#                   and NOTHING else ('localhost' does not match 'a.localhost');
#                 * a SUFFIX '*.suffix': matches exactly one label under the
#                   suffix ('*.example.com' matches 'a.example.com', NOT
#                   'example.com' itself, NOT 'a.b.example.com').
#               Any other shape is REFUSED: coverage nobody stated is a
#               silent allow-all.
#   argclass    the lexicon proper-noun SURFACE of the class (sort `argclass`).
#   protected   yes | no   (yes -> the seat injects protected(<class>)).
# AN UNCLASSED AUTHORITY IS REFUSED BY NAME (unclassed-arg), nothing executes:
# the operator does not have to enumerate what is forbidden, because anything
# they have not classified is not permitted.  An IP-literal authority can
# never match a host pattern, so it is unclassable BY CONSTRUCTION.
# THE SHIPPED STATE IS FAIL-CLOSED: the one row below classes a DOCUMENTATION
# example host as PROTECTED, and authorizes NOTHING.  To let http_get fetch a
# real host, the operator adds a row classing that host as a NON-protected
# argclass (a re-pin release) — and that grant is a capability increase the
# log makes visible, exactly like a new write alias.
example.com
